en: Itivuttaka 31 Dukanipāta, Paṭhamavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and went into his dwelling. Thereupon, the venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to the Blessed One: “‘The one who is not easy to correct,’ it was said by the Blessed One. In what way, Bhante, is a person ‘not easy to correct’? “A person, Ānanda, is not easy to correct when they do not accept instruction, do not listen to advice, and do not attend upon those who are more learned. In this way, Ānanda, a person is ‘not easy to correct. “The one who is easy to correct,” it was said by the Blessed One. In what way, Bhante, is a person “easy to correct”? “A person, Ānanda, is easy to correct when they accept instruction, listen to advice, and attend upon those who are more learned. In this way, Ānanda, a person is ‘easy to correct. “Just as, Ānanda, a person who has been struck with a poisoned arrow might say: ‘I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know who struck me, whether he is a noble, a brahmin, a merchant, or a worker; whether he is tall, short, or of medium height; whether he is dark, fair, or ruddy-skinned; whether he comes from such a village, town, or city; and what kind of bow, bowstring, shaft, feather, and arrowhead he used. That person would die before such matters could be known. So too, Ānanda, a person who does not accept instruction, does not listen to advice, and does not attend upon those who are more learned is called ‘one who is not easy to correct. But just as a person struck with a poisoned arrow would think: ‘Let me first have this arrow pulled out, and then I shall learn who struck me—whether he is a noble, a brahmin, a merchant, or a worker; whether he is tall, short, or of medium height; whether he is dark, fair, or ruddy-skinned; whether he comes from such a village, town, or city; and what kind of bow, bowstring, shaft, feather, and arrowhead he used. That person would not die before such matters are known. So too, Ānanda, a person who accepts instruction, listens to advice, and attends upon those who are more learned is called ‘one who is easy to correct. “Just as, Ānanda, a person who has been struck with a poisoned arrow might say: ‘I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the clan of the one who struck me; their name and family; their appearance; their height; their gait; their voice; their strength; their skill; their age; and the exact spot where the arrow struck. That person would die before such matters could be known. So too, Ānanda, a person who does not accept instruction, does not listen to advice, and does not attend upon those who are more learned is called ‘one who is not easy to correct. But just as a person struck with a poisoned arrow would think: ‘Let me first have this arrow pulled out, and then I shall learn the clan of the one who struck me; their name and family; their appearance; their height; their gait; their voice; their strength; their skill; their age; and the exact spot where the arrow struck. That person would not die before such matters are known. So too, Ānanda, a person who accepts instruction, listens to advice, and attends upon those who are more learned is called ‘one who is easy to correct. “Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will accept instruction, we will listen to advice, and we will attend upon those who are more learned. Thus, Ānanda, should you train yourselves.”
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:

Here, monks, a certain person has performed what is beautiful, performed what is wholesome, provided a refuge for those who are afraid; he has not performed evil, he has not performed cruelty, he has not committed a foul deed.
He does not burn with the thought, “I have done what is beautiful,” nor does he burn with the thought, “I have not done what is evil.”
“Monks, these two things are not conducive to remorse.
Thus the Blessed One spoke. With regard to this, it is said:
And whatever else is associated with hatred—
having refrained from unwholesome action and having performed much wholesome action;
"With the breakup of the body, the wise one is reborn in heaven.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
